questions.q: True or false? Our two strikers can press all three of Blue's backs alone.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. Two strikers cannot reach three backs, so a midfielder must help at the right time.
choiceExplanations: Count them: two strikers against three backs. One back always has time on the ball.
Right, it's false. Two strikers cannot reach three backs, so a midfielder must help at the right time.

questions.q: Blue's back receives close to our right midfielder. Which picture adds the third presser safely?
options: Central midfielder goes to the ball
Right midfielder presses, two stay inside
questions.explain: Yes. The nearest midfielder presses, and the other two close the inside lanes behind.
choiceExplanations: The central midfielder is far away, and the middle is left open behind.
Yes. The nearest midfielder presses, and the other two close the inside lanes behind.
Nobody protects behind, so one pass inside beats the whole midfield.

questions.q: Now Blue's other back receives close to our left midfielder, with cover inside. What happens next?
options: Left midfielder holds with the midfield
Central midfielder runs out to press
questions.explain: Yes. The back is close and the cover is ready, so the nearest midfielder presses.
choiceExplanations: Yes. The back is close and the cover is ready, so the nearest midfielder presses.
Holding fits a far pass. This back is close and our cover is ready, so press.
That leaves the middle open. The left midfielder is much closer to the ball.
